display.title: Rashi's Father and the Precious Diamond
display.summary_short: A Yiddish story for grandchildren: Rashi's poor father would not sell a precious diamond for an idol, and was blessed with a son who would light up the world with Torah.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish by a grandmother to her grandchildren. It is just before Pesach, and Rashi's parents are so poor that they have nothing for Yom Tov and long for a child. Davening by the sea, Rashi's father finds a huge diamond. A jeweler values it at a hundred thousand thalers and says the local poritz needs it for the eye of an idol. Rashi's father refuses to let it serve idol worship, but fears the poritz's anger, so he offers to show the poritz the diamond on his ship, where it 'falls' into the sea. The poritz sends him home empty-handed, and Rashi's parents rejoice that they were saved from helping idol worship, even if they stay poor. That night an angel tells him that, in reward, he and his wife will have a son who will light up the whole world with his Torah: Rashi, whom every child and adult learns with the Chumash. The grandmother ends by praising each grandchild's good behavior and asking them to listen to their parents and make them happy.
display.lesson: Never give up a mitzvah for money; Hashem rewards those who stay loyal to Him. Children who listen to their parents bring them joy.
